column1: 1. Almost all the fresher jobs I can legally collect sit on ONE platform
column2: 865 of 910 published posts (95%) come from Unstop. The big job sites do not give automated access: LinkedIn's robots.txt says 'Disallow: /', Glassdoor and Internshala disallow their job pages, SmartRecruiters' API says 'Disallow: /' for every bot except LinkedIn's, and Naukri's robots.txt returned HTTP 403 to my bot. Unstop's robots.txt explicitly allows /api/public/*. I did not check Indeed's terms of service, so I left Indeed out as a precaution.
column3: Where: the robots.txt file of each site (fetched on the date shown), and the source split on the live page. Why it matters: 'collect 200+ real posts from public sources and respect each site's terms' is only possible because of one student platform. If Unstop changes its rules, this tool loses 95% of its data, and a product built on fresher jobs should plan for that.

column1: 2. Company career pages add few fresher posts, and guessing company pages gives wrong matches
column2: On the 31 company job boards I use, 1,095 jobs are in India but only 62 (5.7%) are entry-level. An earlier probe of my first 20 hand-picked boards gave 87 of 812 (about 11%). Separately, my company finder matched the wrong company for 11 of 39 boards (28%): 'Porter' was a US nurse-staffing board, 'Navi' a San Francisco hardware startup, 'Slice' a team hiring in North Macedonia. Fix: keep a board only if it has at least one India-located job.
column3: Where: the public Greenhouse, Lever and Ashby job-board APIs, counted per board; the finder's own log (pipeline/discover.py). Why it matters: most hiring pages are built for experienced hires, so a fresher job tool cannot rely on company career pages. And 'looks like the right company' is not proof: without the India-job check, wrong companies would have been shown to students.
column4: Tab 'Evidence - boards' (total / India / entry-level jobs for every board). Tab 'Run stats'. Dropped boards: slice, pine, porter (Greenhouse and Lever), cloudflare, fi, navi, ditto, pocket, tiger, leap. Code: pipeline/discover.py.

column1: 3. An LLM tags role and city cheaply and well, but is weakest at judging experience level
column2: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite cost about $0.15 per 1,000 posts (1,011 posts, $0.15 total). On 50 random posts: role 94%, city 92%, fresher flag 88% (strict; lenient 100% / 100% / 96%). The model also removed 27 of 936 posts (2.9%) that Unstop had labelled fresher but that needed more experience. Its errors: it marked a '3-4 years' Sales Executive as fresher-friendly and rejected a 'Freshers to 6 years' post.
column3: Where: the tagging runs (token counts and cost are logged on every run) and my read of 50 posts against their full text. Why it matters: tags are cheap enough to run daily on everything, but the experience-level call is the one that decides whether a student sees a job that fits them, so it needs a human check or a stricter rule next.
